- ⟨pattern⟩ `agents/*/*.md`: agents/<department>/<id>.md with frontmatter `name` (equal to the file stem and the team.json id) and `description` (at most 300 characters, with a trigger clause such as 'Use when...' or 'Activate when...' and an exclusion clause 'Not for ... (use <id>)'). Core roles follow the shape of agents/engineering/fullstack-engineer.md (## Mission, ## Expertise, ## Operating protocol, ## Collaboration, ## Skills you lean on, ## Guardrails, ## Self-learning, ## Output contract). Specialists use exactly ## When, ## Inputs, ## Procedure, ## Output, ## Done when, ## Hand-offs, ## Access in that order, as in agents/specialists/sre-engineer.md. The roster lint also requires: a compiled prompt of 400 to 2500 tokens; none of the retired terms it bans (task board, task evidence record, status.md, plan.md, qa.md, lessons.md, decisions.md, hardening, wcag 2.1, phase gate, '## standing orders', 'phase <n>', 'ship phase'); exactly one **Owns:** line across all roles for each lifecycle artifact, with fixed owners (ceo: BRIEF.md, ASSUMPTIONS.md, DELIVERY-REPORT.md; product-manager: PRD.md; cto-architect: ARCHITECTURE.md; ux-ui-designer: DESIGN.md; delivery-lead: READINESS.md, RETROSPECTIVE.md; qa-lead: VERIFICATION.md; release-manager: RELEASE.md; cmo: MARKETING.md), and no **Owns:** line in read-only or research roles; and only known role ids in backticks. A new role also needs its team.json entry (with activate_when for a specialist), the README counts, roster.json in team.json order, a guide rebuild, and regenerated golden files if it is in helpers.GOLDEN_ROSTER. Department folders: leadership, engineering, support, marketing, specialists.
- ⟨pattern⟩ `protocols/*.md`: One Markdown protocol linked from runtime/templates/router.md or protocols/agent-contract.md (an unlinked protocol is never read by an agent). It names sibling protocols by bare filename and installed paths as .agentic-team/..., and is scanned for retired vocabulary (test_law) and overclaims (test_release).

- ⟨pattern⟩ `runtime/templates/*.md`: One Markdown template, filled in one of five ways, so check which before editing. (1) Artifact templates registered in ARTIFACT_TEMPLATES (assumptions, brief, delivery-report, prd, readiness, release, retrospective, risks, verification) are copied by `scaffold`, which replaces only `{{project}}`. (2) task.md, stage-context.md, fusion-brief.md, fusion-proposal.md and fusion-critique.md are filled with str.format: use `{field}` names and double any literal brace. (3) fusion-dissent.md has `{{council}}` replaced. (4) fusion-synthesis.md and fusion-decision.md are copied as they are. (5) adr.md, checkpoint.md and handoff.md are forms agents copy by hand, referenced from protocols/communication.md and the agentic-build skill. router.md is installed verbatim as .agentic-team/AGENTS.md. Every template must be referenced from the CLI or from shared law (test_law).
- ⟨pattern⟩ `skills/*/SKILL.md`: skills/<name>/SKILL.md with frontmatter `name` equal to the folder (lowercase words joined by hyphens), `description` longer than 80 and at most 1024 characters, and `compatibility` (required, at most 500 characters). The body is a runbook with exact `.agentic-team/bin/agentic_team.py` commands and no TODO. Every skill folder also needs agents/openai.yaml. Only folders belong directly under skills/: a stray file there breaks the skill checks and ships into every install (D11). A skill that a workflow runs also needs team.json workflows.<id>.skill set to skills/<name>.
- ⟨pattern⟩ `skills/*/agents/openai.yaml`: YAML with interface.display_name, interface.short_description, interface.default_prompt (which must contain `$<skill-name>`) and policy.allow_implicit_invocation; copy skills/agentic-build/agents/openai.yaml. policy.allow_implicit_invocation is optional; the three shipped skills that set it set false.
- ⟨pattern⟩ `skills/*/references/*.md`: One Markdown reference that its SKILL.md links to; scanned for retired vocabulary like all shared law.
- ⟨pattern⟩ `tests/test_*.py`: A unittest module that imports from helpers (`import helpers` or `from helpers import ...`) before anything uses the CLI, because that import isolates AGENTIC_TEAM_HOME. It uses helpers.team, helpers.fresh_project() and helpers.run_cli() instead of the real home or source tree, and reads expected values from team.json or config/ instead of literal counts (several existing tests still hard-code them, GAP-1). New shared fixtures go in helpers.py; test_installers reuses shells() from test_repairs_packets.
- ⟨pattern⟩ `tests/golden/**`: Never written by hand. After a compiler change, regenerate with `UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_safety_net.py"` (PowerShell: `$env:UPDATE_GOLDEN=1; python -m unittest ...`; cmd: `set UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 && python -m unittest ...`) and review the diff; the role set is fixed in helpers.GOLDEN_ROSTER. Files under nested .claude/, .codex/ and .agentic-team/ folders are invisible to this blueprint (D6).
- ⟨pattern⟩ `evals/scenarios/*.json`: A JSON object with name, description and steps (optional harness and preset), using only the step forms documented at the top of evals/run_scenarios.py (cli, human, write, state, task, exec_py, python). Together the scenario names must cover greenfield, plan-given, brownfield, fusion, rejection and self-approval (test_evals). File names use snake_case (plan_given.json); the `name` field uses kebab-case (plan-given-hitl-bmad) and is what the coverage check matches.

- ⟨pattern⟩ `knowledge/playbooks/*.md`: knowledge/playbooks/<role-id>.md created from _template.md, headed `# Playbook — <role-id>`, with checks under ## Before starting, ## While building and ## Before claiming done. Seeded checks end with `<!-- status: baseline -->`. Lines an agent adds use the candidate form from knowledge/playbooks/README.md: `- [ ] <imperative check>  <!-- status: candidate · learned: YYYY-MM-DD · source: <run>/<task> · cost: <what it broke> -->`. Promoting a candidate to baseline is the owner's decision (protocols/evolution.md). About forty lines at most.
- ⟨pattern⟩ `docs/*-plan.md`: A plan with scope, phases, acceptance and risks, registered in docs/agent-team-guide/documents.json under current or earlier together with its prompt; an unregistered plan fails the guide check.
- ⟨pattern⟩ `docs/*-prompt.md`: One ready-to-paste prompt for a single plan, registered beside that plan in documents.json.
- ⟨pattern⟩ `docs/*-prompts.md`: Ready-to-paste prompts, one per phase of a plan, registered beside that plan in documents.json.
- ⟨pattern⟩ `docs/*-progress.md`: A dated log of phases completed, deviations and evidence for one plan; facts only, never a claim that a plan passed.
